_comment: #475 ground-floor slotting. The constraint the schema imposes: _exactMarks is written by
PlaceExact and read by PlaceProcedural, so exclusion runs exact -> procedural ONLY. Two
procedural rules are blind to each other and RuleJson has no 'exclusive with rule N' field.
A floor therefore supports any number of exacts (the author separates their x by hand) plus
at most ONE rule that dodges them. Floor 0 spends that budget on door (exact) + garage (rule);
floors 1..8 spend it on bay (exact) + window (rule). No windows on floor 0 - a Victorian
ground floor IS the garage and the entry.
The garage is a rule, not an exact, because a rule can be gated on facade width and an exact
cannot. PlaceProcedural derives count = floor(spanMeters / spacing) before countMin/countMax,
so countMin 0 + spacingMeters 4.0 across a 0.76 span means no garage at all below 5.26 m, and
countMax 1 means never more than one above it. avoidExact then suppresses the remaining slot
whenever it lands within minSpacingMeters 2.0 of the door - i.e. below 5.13 m. Both gates sit
above the 4.90 m at which a 2.53 m garage and a 1.29 m door would actually touch, so the pair
cannot overlap at any facade width. Measured over the 990 buildings in chunks_wintest with a
usable front facade: 671 get a garage (67.8%), 319 get a door alone, 0 overlap.
#471 recommended minSpacingMeters 6.0; that was measured here to suppress the garage below a
16.7 m frontage, i.e. on every real building in the play area, because the same number is both
the exclusion radius and (via max(spacingMeters, minSpacingMeters)) the count divisor.
The bay is an exact at floor 1, centred over the garage - the Victorian bay-over-garage. It
spans 2 floors but _exactMarks is keyed (edge_index, floor) and carries no floorsSpanned, so
floor 2 gets no mark; and even on floor 1 the window rule can only exclude 2.20 m (its repeat
pitch - past that, PlaceProcedural's spacing = max(spacingMeters, minSpacingMeters) would thin
the windows) where clearing a 3.80 m bay needs 2.45 m. Both leave window geometry inside the
bay shell, where it is occluded rather than interpenetrating; it costs triangles, not looks.
Both gaps are tracked as #491.
